```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# MLB Pitch Clock Analysis: T-tests on Total Pitches per Pitcher (2022–2024)
# ------------------------------------------------------------
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load dataset
pitches <- read_csv("Unnecessary Documents/total pitches 2022-2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Peek at column names
glimpse(pitches)

# If necessary, rename for consistency:
# For example, if your file columns are: pitcher, team, year, n
# pitches <- pitches %>% rename(Pitcher = pitcher, Year = year, Total_Pitches = n)

# 2. Check summary by season
summary_stats <- pitches %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pitchers = n(),
    mean_pitches = mean(n, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_pitches = sd(n, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
print(summary_stats)

# 3. Run t-tests
# Compare 2022 vs 2023
t_22_23 <- t.test(n ~ year, data = filter(pitches, year %in% c(2022, 2023)))

# Compare 2023 vs 2024
t_23_24 <- t.test(n ~ year, data = filter(pitches, year %in% c(2023, 2024)))

# Compare 2022 vs 2024 (optional)
t_22_24 <- t.test(n ~ year, data = filter(pitches, year %in% c(2022, 2024)))

# 4. Print results
cat("\n--- T-Test Results ---\n")
cat("\n2022 vs 2023:\n")
print(t_22_23)

cat("\n2023 vs 2024:\n")
print(t_23_24)

cat("\n2022 vs 2024:\n")
print(t_22_24)

# 5. Boxplot for visualization
ggplot(pitches, aes(x = factor(year), y = n)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Total Pitches per Pitcher by Season",
       x = "Season",
       y = "Total Pitches") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)


```

```{r}
t_22_23 <- t.test(n ~ year, data = filter(pitches, year %in% c(2022, 2023)))
cat("\n2022 vs 2023:\n")
print(t_22_23)
```
